description: Canonical controlled vocabulary for confidence dimensions, qualitative confidence levels, and confidence interpretation within A.R.I.A. Confidence represents trust in the quality, support, reliability, calibration, sufficiency, or applicability of information or reasoning. Confidence is explicitly distinct from probability.

confidence_contract.higher_value_meaning: Greater confidence in the quality, support, reliability, sufficiency, calibration, or applicability represented by the specified confidence dimension.
confidence_contract.probability_separation: A confidence value shall never be interpreted as the probability that a hypothesis, diagnosis, event, failure mode, or outcome is true.
confidence_contract.precision_rule: Confidence values shall not imply greater precision than the underlying evidence, validation, provenance, or reasoning supports.
confidence_contract.dimension_rule: Confidence shall identify its applicable dimension whenever collapsing multiple dimensions into one value would hide material uncertainty.

confidence_dimensions.description: Confidence in the technical quality, integrity, completeness, directness, and usability of an evidence item or evidence set.
Confidence that a source or source-derived representation reliably preserves and communicates the technical information attributed to it.
Confidence that information extracted from an artifact or source accurately represents the underlying source content.
Confidence in the support, fidelity, and technical defensibility of a claim while preserving the distinction between the claim and canonical technical truth.
Confidence in the support for a semantic relationship between eligible canonical A.R.I.A. objects.
Confidence that retrieved knowledge, evidence, experience, source material, or technical relationships are sufficiently applicable to the current technical context.
Confidence that the available evidence sufficiently supports the current diagnostic conclusion or diagnostic state.
Confidence that the evidence supports a causal attribution rather than mere association, correlation, temporal proximity, or symptom improvement.
Confidence that the technical problem has actually been resolved and is not merely temporarily improved, masked, bypassed, or insufficiently retested.
Confidence that a validation procedure and its resulting evidence adequately test the technical assertion, corrective action, diagnosis, or resolution being evaluated.
Confidence that validated historical information is sufficiently reliable, attributable, contextualized, and generalizable to influence future A.R.I.A. reasoning.
Confidence in the quality and support of a canonical entity assertion, classification, or identity resolution.
Confidence that an alternate term, abbreviation, manufacturer term, historical term, or spelling correctly resolves to a particular canonical entity in the applicable context.
Confidence that a measured value adequately represents the physical or logical quantity it purports to measure.
Confidence that a human or system observation accurately represents what was actually observed.
Confidence in an A.R.I.A. model-assisted interpretation, classification, extraction, normalization, or proposed inference before structured validation and acceptance.

qualitative_levels.description: Confidence has not been established or cannot currently be meaningfully estimated.
qualitative_levels.reasoning_policy: Preserve the unknown state. Do not manufacture a numeric confidence value.

qualitative_levels.description: Support is weak, incomplete, materially uncertain, or significantly contradicted.
qualitative_levels.reasoning_policy: Treat conclusions as highly tentative and prioritize discriminating information where technically worthwhile.

qualitative_levels.description: Some support exists, but material uncertainty, incompleteness, applicability concerns, or contradictions remain.
qualitative_levels.reasoning_policy: Avoid strong conclusions where additional high-value validation is reasonably available.

qualitative_levels.description: Meaningful support exists, but uncertainty remains sufficient to limit certainty or generalization.
qualitative_levels.reasoning_policy: Use the conclusion with explicit uncertainty and seek further discrimination when the decision impact warrants it.

qualitative_levels.description: Strong support exists with limited material uncertainty or contradiction.
qualitative_levels.reasoning_policy: The conclusion may normally guide technical action while preserving applicable residual uncertainty.

qualitative_levels.description: Support is exceptionally strong, well validated, and highly consistent within the applicable technical context.
qualitative_levels.reasoning_policy: Treat as strongly supported while preserving the possibility of revision if materially better evidence appears.

aggregation_rules.rule: Confidence dimensions shall remain independently representable when combining them would hide materially different uncertainty.
A composite confidence value may be calculated only by an explicitly identified method. The Registry does not prescribe a universal averaging formula.
The lowest material confidence dimension may constrain a conclusion when that dimension is required for the conclusion to be technically defensible.
High confidence in one dimension shall not silently compensate for a critical unknown in another dimension.
Confidence aggregation shall account for dependence. Multiple records derived from one underlying source shall not be treated as independent confidence contributions.

semantic_rules.rule: Confidence and probability are separate quantities. Hypothesis probability shall not appear as a confidence dimension.
A hypothesis may have high probability and low confidence when available information favors it but the evidence base is weak.
A hypothesis may have low probability while confidence in that probability estimate is high when strong evidence consistently disfavors it.

Source authority and source reliability are separate. An authoritative source may be poorly applicable or incorrectly extracted, while a reliable field observation may not be authoritative for design intent.

Diagnostic confidence, causal confidence, and resolution confidence shall remain distinguishable. Knowing what condition exists, knowing what caused it, and knowing that it has been resolved are different conclusions.
Symptom improvement shall not automatically produce high causal confidence.
Successful corrective action may increase causal confidence only to the degree that the action discriminates the suspected cause from plausible alternatives.
Repeated historical occurrence may increase confidence in an empirical pattern but does not independently prove a deterministic causal relationship.
Unknown confidence is a valid state and shall not automatically be converted to zero confidence.
Zero confidence and unknown confidence are different. Zero is an assessed value; unknown means no defensible value has been established.
A confidence value of 1.0 shall not be interpreted as philosophical certainty or immunity from revision.
Model interpretation confidence describes confidence in the model-assisted interpretation itself and does not grant the model authority to persist canonical truth.
Confidence shall be recalculated when material evidence, provenance, applicability, validation, or contradiction state changes.
Qualitative labels are human-readable interpretations of normalized confidence values and shall not replace the underlying numeric value when a numeric value has been validly calculated.
Confidence shall never be increased merely because the same underlying information was copied, summarized, transformed, or represented multiple times.
Confidence used for learning shall reflect whether the historical information is safe to influence future reasoning, not merely whether the historical case was closed.

prohibited_uses: Using confidence as a substitute for source authority.
Using confidence as a substitute for technical applicability.
Treating an unknown confidence value as zero.
Treating duplicate source representations as independent corroboration.
Treating a qualitative confidence label as an independent runtime state machine.
Encoding case lifecycle states in this Registry.
Encoding decision states in this Registry.
Allowing model-generated confidence to establish authoritative state without structured validation.
Using one generic confidence score when materially different confidence dimensions must remain visible.
